## Building canvas-native agents: lessons from Laya

• What we observed in testing

At Luma, we’re building canvas-native agents that can read and understand a creative workspace and work within it. On a board in progress, references sit beside generated variations, notes capture decisions, and frames and groups bring ideas together for comparison. An agent needs that context to help with the work.

When a creative working on an ad asks, “Bring these campaign directions together, keeping the variations with their references, and lay them out side by side for review,” the agent needs to identify those relationships and preserve them as it changes the layout.

Laya, our canvas-organization subagent, gave us a practical test of this approach. We extended the view of Orca, Luma’s main agent, to include canvas objects and their relationships alongside media. Here we describe how agents read the board, how Orca hands work to Laya, and how layout code checks and applies changes while people keep working on the canvas.

## Reading the canvas

An agent reviewing that campaign needs the cues humans would use: frame titles, membership, and nearby notes. Reading the canvas means exposing those objects and relationships alongside the media assets.

An early bug showed why the read layer mattered. Frame names visible to users were missing from some agent-facing reads because the code checked for a different shape type. The model could not use names it never received; we had to fix the representation.

Shared finding and search tools expose JSON views at several levels of detail: compact rows to survey results, detailed cards to inspect an item, and references to identify it across calls. These connect media with canvas objects and their relationships, giving the agent a path from discovery to inspection and action:

The agent can inspect individual items or expand a container without reading every detail on the board. Parent–child relationships give it a tree-like view of pages, frames, and their contents, so membership need not be inferred from proximity. Screenshots alone do not provide the explicit identities and relationships needed for precise edits.

During execution, version checks prevent Laya from combining pages of a snapshot taken from different board states, and tool receipts report what changed.

## Why a subagent

With that shared read foundation, Orca, Luma’s main agent, can delegate organization to Laya as a specialist subagent. Orca passes the user’s intent, permitted scope, and constraints; Laya gathers the board detail it needs, plans and applies changes, and reports the outcome back. The server captures the scope and saves a layout recovery snapshot before the job starts.

This main-agent/subagent structure gives organization its own working context. Descriptions, grouping decisions, plans, and write receipts stay with the specialist instead of filling Orca’s ongoing conversation. It also lets us customize Laya’s tools, instructions, and model configuration independently as we learn what works for different organizing tasks.

The cost of the split is the handoff. Laya does not rely on the full conversation, so Orca must include the relevant constraints and any asset names the user has confirmed. If the scope omits a destination frame the user intended, Laya cannot simply treat it as editable. It must work within the permitted scope or report what remains unresolved.

## Planning and placement

The model decides what belongs together and in what order; code decides where it goes. Laya builds on our shared canvas placement engine, which already supported relative placement and auto-layout. We extended that foundation for frame growth and collision-aware placement, then added section plans to coordinate layout within and across sections.

In one paired test of the same scoped-layout request, runtime fell from 195 to 22 seconds and committed write batches from 12 to one after a fix to parent-local coordinates and measured text bounds.

Operation batches remain available for direct moves and other supported edits; section plans provide a higher-level option for organization.

A simplified plan illustrates the boundary; these names stand in for actual item references:

{ "plan": [ { "section": "References", "items": ["inspiration_post", "product_photo"] }, { "section": "Product A", "items": ["first_try", "variation", "selected"] } ] }

In this example, the model places the product photo with the references and the selected variation after the earlier attempts. The layout engine uses measured item sizes to calculate rows, spacing, and coordinates. Titles and annotations can be included in the plan.

Tool contracts matter too. Malformed reference lists and unsupported parameters caused retries in early runs. We normalized inputs where intent was unambiguous and improved refusal messages so the agent could correct a request. Batching related edits reduces the number of calls, but does not eliminate invalid plans.

## Editing a shared board

Understanding an item does not grant permission to edit it. Laya works within a permitted scope, but moving selected items can require checked adjustments to surrounding containers. On a shared canvas, even edits to different items can compete for space. Deciding when to preserve nearby placements, adjust them, or ask for broader scope remains an evolving product and engineering challenge.

The server applies changes in checked, bounded batches. A batch commits as a unit; an organizing run can contain several batches, so an interrupted run can leave useful work already applied. Locks and checks for items moved or resized during the run protect user placements. Newly added items remain outside the captured scope and can be organized in a later pass.

تشرح Luma كيف تبني «وكلاء أصليين للوحة العمل» يقرؤون المساحة الإبداعية بما فيها الوسائط والإطارات والملاحظات والعلاقات بينها ويعملون داخلها.

• جُرّب النهج مع Laya، وكيل فرعي لتنظيم اللوحة يفوّضه إليه Orca، الوكيل الرئيسي.
• يمرر Orca نية المستخدم والنطاق المسموح، ثم يقرأ Laya اللوحة ويخطط التجميعات ويطبق التغييرات.
• النموذج يقرر ما ينتمي معاً، بينما يتولى الكود تحديد المواضع بدقة.
• تُنفَّذ التغييرات على دفعات مفحوصة مع لقطات تدعم التراجع.
• في مقارنة عمياء صغيرة فضّل المراجعون سير العمل مع Laya.
• ترتيب لوحات القصة المصورة ما زال يحتاج تحسيناً.

أهمية الخبر: يوضح دروساً عملية في تصميم وكلاء يعملون على مساحات إبداعية.
